podcast.body: Debbie Harry was invited by Italian producer Giorgio Moroder to contribute to the soundtrack for Paul Schrader's 1980 film *American Gigolo*. Moroder had originally offered the song to Stevie Nicks, but she was unavailable, leading him to invite Harry to finish the lyrics and record it. Despite minor contributions from other Blondie members, the song was released as a Blondie single and exploded onto the charts, reaching number one on the Hot 100 for six straight weeks after two months, and was named the top song of 1980 by Billboard. "Call me, a song quite literally about a Jigalo's lifestyle, was full of sleaze and strut."

podcast.body: This dance rock classic, written and produced by Giorgio Moroder and sung by Debbie Harry (the "diva of CBGB"), was featured on the soundtrack to the Richard Gere movie "American Gigolo." It spent six weeks at the top of the Hot 100, demonstrating how dance music could transition into a new decade even as disco's popularity waned. "Call Me spent six weeks on top of the Hot 100 and showed how dance music, even as disco was ebbing in popularity, could make the transition into a new decade."
